PATCH_028: cross-product regression audit (00_Installer/01_Planning/02_Evaluation/03_Compare) found this product's schema_version had drifted from the shared Core Project JSON Schema '3.0' to an internal product-version-like value ('1.0.632' in VERSION.json, '1.0.620' default in core/version.py); both corrected to '3.0' to match 02_Evaluation/03_Compare. PATCH_029: added a staleness warning for the north-rotation (北方位) input field in module1/app.py. Typing a new value into the field, or saving the project, updates common.north_rotation_deg but does not by itself re-run PDF analysis or update the orientation-dependent drawing_analysis/profile/quantity_takeoff fields (those are only set inside run() when "解析を実行" executes analyze_pdf()); a user could type a rotation, save, and reasonably but incorrectly believe it had been applied. Added self._north_last_analyzed_value/_known, updated whenever run() completes an analysis pass and restored from the saved drawing_analysis.north_rotation_input_deg when a Project JSON is reopened (restore_saved_state). A new label (self.north_stale_label) below the north entry, and an orange highlight on the entry itself, appear via a StringVar trace (_update_north_staleness_warning) whenever the current field value differs from that baseline, asking the user to run "解析を実行" again; no warning is shown before any analysis has ever been run (nothing to compare against yet). Verified under Xvfb: no warning on a brand-new unanalyzed project even after typing a value; a reopened project whose field matches its last analysis shows no warning; editing the field then shows the warning and orange highlight, which clears when the value is reverted; blank/unparseable input normalizes to the same None baseline as an unanalyzed blank field so it does not spuriously warn.

PATCH_030: added the missing electrical/mechanical/plumbing equipment-schedule (機器リスト) extraction Module 1 never had. A cross-module audit against a real S-Structure_Sample project had found that document_wide_preflight scanned every page of registered MEP drawings, but quantity_takeoff never produced a single hvac/electrical row (equipment_symbol_recognition stayed null, mep_route_quantity_reconciliation found 0 physical owners) because no extraction step existed to read the schedule tables at all -- only downstream route-reconciliation and cost-linkage contracts were in place, with nothing feeding them. Added _extract_mep_equipment_facts (deterministic text scan, same style as the existing _extract_joinery_facts, anchored on "機器リスト（…設備）" section headers, reading each row's 台数 column as the last standalone integer before the 参考型番/location text so electrical codes like "3-200" and power figures like "1.37" are never mistaken for quantity) and _merge_mep_equipment_inventory, wired into run() right after project_evidence is collected and before the mep_trade keyword classifier runs, so newly merged rows are tagged hvac/plumbing/electrical/fire automatically with no change needed to that classifier. Reads registered PDFs directly via extract_pdf_text (added _collect_mep_equipment_source_text) rather than through _collect_registered_project_pdf_evidence's shared per-page text, whose embedded+OCR merge places roughly one token per line and is unusable for this extractor's whole-row matching; also added a mep_text discipline-scoped field to that shared evidence collector for other future consumers, mirroring the existing joinery_text/structural_text fields, though this extractor does not depend on it. Verified against the real uploaded 機械設備図/電気設備図 PDFs end-to-end through the actual Module1App methods (not just a standalone script): all 21 mechanical/plumbing equipment rows extracted with correct quantities and locations (GHP x7, EF/VF fans x8, HEX heat exchangers x3, DP-1, OTU-1, GW-1), correctly merged into quantity_takeoff.rows, and correctly classified downstream into mep_cost_linkage.trade_row_counts as hvac=18/plumbing=3/electrical=0 -- electrical=0 confirmed correct rather than a bug, since this project's electrical PDF genuinely has no 機器リスト-style table (only 特記仕様書 boilerplate); the extractor will pick up an electrical schedule automatically on a future drawing set that does include one. Confirmed no regression via dev_checks/ (all 15 pass) and an unchanged pyflakes warning set.

PATCH_031: fixed the same root cause found in PATCH_030 (MEP equipment extraction) for joinery (建具表) area extraction. _extract_joinery_facts matches a symbol and its W×H dimensions within the same text line, but joinery_text (built by _collect_registered_project_pdf_evidence from the shared embedded+OCR per-page merge) was confirmed against this project's real 建具表 to place roughly one token per line, scattering a schedule row's symbol away from its dimensions; only 1 of 9 window/door codes (AW-2) ever resolved an area, the rest silently fell back to existence-only rows (存在確認・外部/内部未確定). Re-read joinery-classified documents with extract_pdf_text (plain page.get_text(), the same fix already used for MEP) before building joinery_text, instead of reusing the shared per-page text. Verified against the real 建築図.pdf: AD-1 now resolves an explicit area (2.22 m², Low-E5+A6+FL6 glazing) and AW-2 improves (21.6 m² / 10枚, up from 6.3 m² / 5枚). Confirmed, and disclosed, a REMAINING separate limitation: 7 of 9 codes (AG-1, AW-1, AW-3, AW-4, AW-5, SD-1, SS-1/SS-2) still resolve existence-only. Their dimensions exist only in the graphical 建具表 (a CAD schedule where each code's W/H figures are drawn as separate dimension-line callouts positioned around a small elevation drawing, not written as adjacent prose text near the symbol anywhere in the document), so no amount of linear/tokenization fixing can recover them; AD-1/AW-2 only resolved because their dimensions happen to ALSO appear as running-text formulas elsewhere (the 採光・換気計算 table's "W(...)×h...×...ヱ" notation). A full fix for the remaining codes needs a position-aware extractor that matches each symbol's table cell to nearby dimension text by page X/Y coordinates, the same class of technique already used for RC/steel member vector takeoff (_fitz_vector_lines_near_title, _word_centers, _nearest_center) but not yet built for joinery schedules; not attempted in this patch. Confirmed no regression via dev_checks/ (all 15 pass) and an unchanged pyflakes warning set.

PATCH_032: built the position-aware (page X/Y coordinate) joinery-schedule dimension extractor that PATCH_031 identified as the remaining fix needed for the 7 window/door/shutter codes whose width/height exist only as CAD dimension-line callouts drawn around each symbol's small elevation picture in the graphical 建具表 (never as adjacent prose text anywhere in the document, so no text-tokenization fix could ever recover them). Added _extract_joinery_dimensions_by_position, using the same class of technique already used elsewhere in this file for RC/steel member vector takeoff: (1) locate each 形状寸法 row-band header, then use the page's own ruling lines (not word positions) to find the shape-drawing region's exact vertical bounds; (2) use the schedule's vertical grid lines for each column's exact X-range; (3) classify every standalone integer in a column as a horizontal-dimension number (bounding box wider than tall) or vertical-dimension number (taller than wide) since CAD dimension text is always rotated to read along its own dimension line, needing no column-position guessing; (4) width/height = the candidate that is a dimension-chain TOTAL (equals the sum of a subset of the other candidates in the same column, e.g. 1800+100+1800=3700 or 425+50+425=900, via new helper _joinery_dimension_chain_total), else width falls back to the largest horizontal candidate and height falls back to the TOPMOST (smallest y) vertical candidate -- verified against every column in this schedule, where an unrelated second/third vertical number is always a sill/floor-reference offset drawn further down, never the item's own opening height. Wired into the existing joinery_facts pipeline: position-based results override a lower-confidence (typically existence-only, confidence 0.58) text-based fact for the same code, and never disturb an already-higher-confidence text-based fact (e.g. AD-1, which already resolved via a different, valid glazing-area calculation elsewhere in the document). Verified against the real 建築図.pdf end-to-end (both the standalone extractor and the full joinery_facts merge): all 7 remaining codes now resolve correct width×height×area — AG-1 3700×400mm=1.48m² (correctly ignoring an unrelated 3000mm wall-height reference line in the same cell), AW-1 3700×1500mm=5.55m², AW-3 1800×800mm=1.44m², AW-4 1200×900mm=1.08m², AW-5 900×900mm=0.81m² (height correctly resolved via the 425+50+425=900 chain, not the naive topmost single value), SD-1 900×2100mm=1.89m², and both SS-1/SS-2 3000×3000mm=9.0m² (a shared drawing correctly applied to both stacked symbols in one schedule cell). Confirmed no regression via dev_checks/ (all 15 pass) and an unchanged pyflakes warning set. Symbol matching intentionally scoped to AW/AD/AG/SD/SS only (matching _extract_joinery_facts' own scope), not LSD/PT interior-door codes, since those already have a separate dedicated extractor (_extract_a12_lsd_opening_inventory) this patch does not touch.

PATCH_033: added extraction for 衛生器具リスト (sanitary fixture schedule) fixture counts -- e.g. 洋風便器, 小便器, カウンター式洗面器, 掃除用流し, キー式散水栓, 洗濯機パン -- the first of three requested follow-ons to PATCH_030 (sanitary fixtures; electrical symbol counts + duct/refrigerant-pipe lengths; HVAC refrigerant/drain-pipe/duct shapes and lengths). Unlike the 機器リスト equipment schedules PATCH_030 handles, this table has no single 台数 column: each fixture row has a 合計 (total) column followed by several per-room breakdown columns (男子トイレ／女子トイレ／機械室／屋外 etc.), and a fixture's name and 合計 number can land in different row-height bins than its breakdown numbers due to multi-line cell wrapping. Added _find_phrase_word_positions (a small reusable helper: unlike PATCH_032's "形状寸法" title, which happened to be one word token, this table's "衛生器具リスト" title is tokenized one character at a time in the source PDF, so phrase matching needs to walk consecutive word tokens rather than assume a single-token heading), _extract_sanitary_fixture_counts (locates the title, finds the repeating row-line PITCH below it via the page's own ruling lines rather than a fixed offset guess, locates the 器具名/合計 column headers to get exact X-ranges, then reads each fixture's 合計 value from a name-anchored row BLOCK so a wrapped multi-row cell still resolves correctly), and _merge_sanitary_fixture_inventory (same row-building pattern as PATCH_030, so the existing mep_trade classifier tags these as plumbing automatically). Verified against the real 機械設備図.pdf end-to-end through the actual Module1App methods: all 7 distinct fixture types resolved with correct counts summed from same-named rows that differ only by size/model (e.g. two 洗面器カウンター installations, W:1800 and W:900, correctly summed to 2 rather than collapsed to 1), total 15 fixtures, and correctly classified into mep_cost_linkage.trade_row_counts as plumbing=7 with no change needed to that classifier. Investigated feasibility for the remaining part of this request -- 給排水管の長さ and 桝/エルボ/チーズ等のジョイント種類・数量 -- and confirmed it needs a fundamentally different technique (tracing pipe-run vector lines for length and matching small graphical joint/fitting icon symbols against the legend on the plumbing plan, not table-header text extraction); not attempted in this patch, reported to the user as a separate, larger follow-on. Confirmed no regression via dev_checks/ (all 15 pass) and an unchanged pyflakes warning set.

PATCH_034: added extraction for 排水桝リスト (drainage manhole/pit schedule) rows -- e.g. ①..⑩ 塩ビ小口径桁 plus 中継槽流入 -- the second concrete win from the user's request for 桁・エルボ・チーズ等のジョイント種類と数量. Same title+ruling-line-pitch+column-header technique as PATCH_381 (_extract_sanitary_fixture_counts), with one added wrinkle: this table's header row is itself exactly one row-pitch tall, so line-pitch alone cannot distinguish the title/header boundary from the header/data boundary; fixed by locating the header LABEL text first (記号/名称/寸法・規格/管低/蓋) within a zone bounded comfortably short of the first data row, then using the ruling line at/below the labels' own bottom edge as the boundary. Added _extract_drainage_manhole_schedule and _merge_drainage_manhole_inventory, wired into run() right after PATCH_381. Found and fixed a real bug during verification: the first implementation bounded the 記号 (symbol) column only by 'anything left of the 名称 column start', which on the full page (not just the isolated table region used during development) swept in unrelated floor-plan text from the rest of the drawing since the table sits on the right side of a much wider page; fixed by locating the 記号 header explicitly and bounding the symbol column between it and the 名称 header, verified via a full-page Module1App smoke test (not just the standalone isolated-region script) that first surfaced the bug. Verified against the real 機械設備図.pdf end-to-end: all 11 rows resolved with correct symbol/name/spec/invert-level/cover detail, correctly classified into mep_cost_linkage.trade_row_counts as plumbing=11. Investigated the user's follow-up correction that elbow/tee/gas-pipe joints DO exist in these drawings (they do): a full text search of the mechanical PDF confirms エルボ/チーズ never appear as text or as a labeled icon anywhere -- P-04's detailed toilet-area routing plan shows only two explicit 'COA100' (掃除口/clean-out) labels, plus many pipe diameter callouts (20/40/50/65/75/100) along routing lines that visibly turn and branch. Elbows and tees in this drawing set are therefore geometric features of the pipe-run lines themselves (a direction-change vertex is an elbow, a 3-way meeting point is a tee), not a separate labeled schedule or icon; extracting them needs vector line-network tracing and vertex classification -- a distinctly different, larger technique from the table extraction this patch and PATCH_381 use, not attempted here and reported to the user as a separate follow-on alongside pipe-run LENGTH (which needs the same underlying route-tracing engine). Confirmed no regression via dev_checks/ (all 15 pass) and an unchanged pyflakes warning set.

PATCH_035: added the first concrete win from Phase 2 of the user's request (electrical symbol counts + duct/refrigerant-pipe lengths): electrical outlet (コンセント) counting. Investigated the full 電気設備図.pdf (13 pages) and found its outlet plan (E-10) labels each outlet directly with plain text on the floor plan itself (２ＥＴ, ２ＥＴ×3, ２ＥＴ・ＷＰ, ２ＥＥＴ×1) rather than a graphical icon needing shape recognition, so this is a simple per-page regex scan (_extract_electrical_outlet_counts) rather than a position-based table read like every other extractor added this session -- parses the ×N multiplier suffix so a label serving several outlets at one spot (２ＥＴ×3 = 3 units) is counted correctly rather than as one occurrence, and only scans pages containing 平面図 (floor plan) to avoid the single-line schematic (E-02) and panel-schedule (E-03) sheets. Added _merge_electrical_outlet_inventory following the same row-building pattern as every other extractor this session. Verified against the real PDF end-to-end through the actual Module1App methods: 37 plain ２ＥＴ, 1 ２ＥＴ・ＷＰ (waterproof), 1 ２ＥＥＴ, correctly classified into mep_cost_linkage.trade_row_counts as electrical=3 (3 label variants) with no change needed to that classifier. Also investigated lighting fixture counting and confirmed it is NOT achievable for this drawing set: unlike outlets, this project's lighting is only grouped by circuit/room in the E-03 panel schedule (電灿 ・事務室・材料試験室他 etc.), with no floor plan itemizing individual fixture locations or counts (only a separate emergency-lighting coverage-radius diagram, E-08, which is a different scope); reported to the user as a genuine data-availability gap rather than a technique limitation.
